verdict.meaning: Five confirmed Low groups remain open. No new serious compromise or wrong deterministic wallet output is established. Successful tests do not erase concrete failures, certify security, prove optimal code or authorize release.

findings.title: Four remaining scratch allocations outlive their private work

reproduction.controls: Correct known phrase/RGB/UTF8 results and preserved borrowed input; original allocations observed transparently, no fake domain rule.

findings.expected: Fresh parser/detection arrays and RGB/UTF8 validation byte scratch are retired after their last private use, on success and refusal. Caller-borrowed arrays and intentionally returned views remain live.
findings.observed: Reading/detecting public index text leaves[0,...,3] in the original parser array even after the EncodedBackup owner is wiped. RGB conversion leaves both real byte arrays nonzero; valid and refused three-byte UTF8 validation leave their original scratch nonzero.
findings.impact: Leaves recoverable numeric indexes or byte fragments in actual mutable allocations after their work has ended. This is a concrete bounded cleanup/conformance defect. It does not demonstrate external exfiltration, spending-authority compromise, a heap-recovery exploit, guaranteed persistence until a particular time, or physical erasure failure.

findings.title: Pinned Shamir recovery drops its reconstructed secret without wiping when the digest fails
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Low, bounded demonstrated impact; no automatic release-blocking exploit is established. This does not grant release approval or waive applicable coding rules.
findings.trigger: A CRC/metadata-valid threshold quorum reaches bc_shamir::recover_secret and interpolation succeeds, but the 32-bit digest comparison fails.

reproduction.method: Exact dependency source/archive proves the missing owner. Coordinator additionally executed the ordinary-index public SSKR construction below against the actual current engine, reaching digest refusal with the healthy literal-entropy control. No freed-memory read or native allocation-observer test was executed.
reproduction.publicConstruction: Use the first two raw payloads of sskrSetVector's 2-of-3 set. For each member x (0 or 1), XOR its first value byte with (x ^ 0xff), keep every other payload byte and metadata unchanged, rebuild its existing CBOR/CRC and encode as UR. This adds the GF(256) degree-one polynomial g(X)=X XOR 255 to only that byte. g(255)=0, so reconstructed S is still the exact public entropy 000102030405060708090a0b0c0d0e0f; g(254)=1, so only the first digest byte changes while its HMAC key stays unchanged. The digest must fail. Submit the two records directly to the actual engine recovery entry.
reproduction.smallestNativeControl: Inside bc-shamir's existing unit-test module, construct S=[0x24;16], D of 16 bytes with D[4..]=0, set D[0..4] to create_digest(D[4..], S)[0..4], then XOR D[0] with 1. recover_secret(&[255,254], &[S,D]) must return ChecksumFailure; it allocates S before the check. Use this only as a small branch control; the above ordinary-index SSKR construction establishes wrapper reachability.
reproduction.qualification: Actual ordinary-index modified quorum reaches native digest refusal and healthy control matches literal public entropy. Missing inner-Vec cleanup is established by exact dependency source/archive, not by inspecting freed/optimized memory.

findings.expected: The reconstructed entropy allocation must have a wiping owner immediately after interpolation, including failed authentication, before any ordinary deallocation.
findings.observed: The pinned source assigns interpolate(...SECRET_INDEX) to a plain Vec<u8> named secret. It memzeros digest and verify, then returns Err(ChecksumFailure) without memzero(secret) or a Zeroizing/Drop owner. The Vec is deallocated normally. SSKR's Zeroizing wrappers cover only successful returned buffers and cannot access this failed internal allocation. Physical residual bytes/optimizer behavior were not measured.
findings.impact: Best-effort secret cleanup fails inside the dependency on a reachable refusal path, despite the first-party/vendored owners correctly retiring their own copies. The construction can make this allocation the correct entropy rather than only a random failed guess. This is a bounded local memory-hygiene defect.

evidence.identity: Cached .crate archive matches Cargo.lock checksum; its shamir.rs member equals the reviewed cache file. interpolate.rs separately read: returns a new ordinary result Vec at lines 143-155.
evidence.nearestTests: Vendored secret.rs Drop-observer tests cover SSKR Secret owners and direct returned bc-shamir buffers, not a buffer lost inside the dependency on ChecksumFailure.
evidence.executionQualification: Original reviewer proposals were static. Coordinator subsequently executed real production-path probes with unchanged source/dist/native inputs, before/after hash manifests, positive/refusal controls and actual-allocation observations. A completed counterexample process is not a passed fix verification.

findings.recommendedFix: Apply an owner-approved pinned dependency fix or minimal reviewed patch making the interpolated secret a zeroizing owner until success transfers it. A wrapper-only wipe cannot reach the allocation. Preserve protocol bytes, attribution and canonical build requirements.

requiredVerification.smallestTest: Add a pre-free test observer to the fixed secret owner, analogous to the existing vendored Secret observer; force the failed-digest branch above and assert zeroization before drop. Keep a literal successful entropy control. Never inspect deallocated storage.

findings.title: The raw SSKR engine accepts a group index outside its declared group count
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Low, bounded demonstrated impact; no automatic release-blocking exploit is established. This does not grant release approval or waive applicable coding rules.
findings.trigger: A transport-valid 1-of-1 record declares groupCount=1 but uses groupIndex=1 (valid indexes for that count contain only 0).

proposedPermanentRegression.method: Exact proposed native regression through the actual bridge decoder, derived by tracing every function body.
proposedPermanentRegression.actualControl: The current source instead returns Ok(vec![0x24;16]). Low-level equivalent: sskr::sskr_combine(&[payload]) succeeds. A valid-control payload changes metadata byte 3 from 0x10 to 0x00 and must keep succeeding.

findings.expected: Reject groupIndex >= groupCount with a stable safe metadata refusal, consistently with Share.info's existing rule. Recorded threshold 1 is intentionally supported, so the fixture is not rejected for an unrelated threshold policy.
findings.observed: The real raw engine and CheckedSskrBridge both recover the literal public 0x24 entropy from groupCount=1/groupIndex=1; groupIndex=0 control also succeeds. The CRC-valid same transport is rejected by JS shareInfo with sskr.transport.invalid-sskr-share-metadata. Source tracing identifies the missing native groupIndex < groupCount guard. This is actual runtime confirmation of the earlier static proposal; the proposed native unit-test insertion itself was not executed.
findings.impact: Consumers of the documented engine API can successfully restore a structurally impossible record that the higher-level library refuses. The issue is input-policy/API inconsistency; the normal CLI/library restore guard remains effective.
